title: Backend entry domain api pagination versioning
topic: Backend entry domain api pagination versioning
question: Why does a list endpoint like GET /posts need pagination, and what are the tradeoffs between offset-based and cursor-based pagination?
idealAnswer:
Without pagination, a growing table means the endpoint eventually returns huge, slow responses and risks timing out or exhausting memory on both server and client

Offset-based pagination (LIMIT/OFFSET) is simple and supports jumping to an arbitrary page, but gets slower as the offset grows (the database still has to scan/skip past all prior rows) and can skip or duplicate items if rows are inserted/deleted between page requests

Cursor-based pagination uses a pointer (often the last seen id or timestamp) to fetch the next page, staying fast regardless of how deep you page, and is stable under concurrent inserts/deletes, but doesn't support jumping to an arbitrary page number

Mentions API versioning at a basic level, e.g. why you'd version an API (URL path like /v1/, or a header) so existing clients don't break when the response shape changes

Bonus: connects pagination choice to the use case, e.g. an admin dashboard with page numbers might prefer offset for UX, an infinite-scroll feed prefers cursor for correctness and performance
